env.#1: What Uplift may move on its own: off, patch, minor or major. Anything larger is proposed in the report.
env.#2: UPLIFT_PHP_MAX: a PHP branch never to go above (e.g. 8.1 on a server held to it). Empty: no ceiling.
env.#3: UPLIFT_OWN_VENDOR: the Composer vendors you publish yourself (e.g. acme, comma-separated); their packages move up to a minor on their own. Empty: none.
env.#4: New features of the installed versions (uplift:adopt): off, propose or apply. UPLIFT_ADOPT_SKIP: adoption ids to leave out.
env.#5: UPLIFT_ADOPT_OPT_IN: adoptions off by default to look for, e.g. readonly-promotion (experimental: can break reflection-based hydration).
env.#6: UPLIFT_SKIP: releases never to move to (package@version, comma-separated), e.g. one that was shipped and rolled back.
env.#7: UPLIFT_HUMAN_VALIDATION: written to report.json for the job that runs Uplift: 1, the upgrade waits for a person; 0, your job may merge it. Uplift itself never merges, pushes or deploys.

post-install-output: * <fg=blue>Uplift</>: see what can move with <comment>php bin/console uplift:plan</>,
and the new features your versions bring with <comment>php bin/console uplift:adopt</>
* Set <comment>UPLIFT_ENABLED=1</> where <comment>uplift:apply</> may change composer.json and composer.lock.
It never pushes or deploys: it leaves a branch and a report (var/uplift/report.md).
